PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Process note:** The Seller's draft labels many clauses [STANDARD], marks them FINAL, and asks that only [OPEN] items be reviewed. Those labels don't bind Wattlebridge, and several [STANDARD] items conflict with our playbook. I've reviewed all 16 issues.

**Authority constraint:** No written authority from Amelia Frost has been given for any fallback. Any concession marked "requires Frost approval" below is off the table until she approves it in writing and identifies the draft.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price, AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer should want:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000 starting position. 20% / AUD 4,800,000 is a conditional fallback only with Frost's written authority.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and counter at 25% / AUD 6M. The 20% figure is a fallback we cannot offer without written authority.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; deductible basket AUD 250,000, recovering only the excess (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer should want:** De minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. The Seller's figures are five times our de minimis and five times our basket, and a deductible structure removes recovery on the first AUD 250,000.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion. Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly excluded (cl 12.3/13).
- **Buyer should want:** 24 months after Completion for general claims. 18 months is a fallback needing Frost's written approval. Limitations must not spread across categories.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the 18-month period and the "applies to all Claims" wording. The second point is a category-separation problem and is addressed under SPA-N-014.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity" (cl 9.3/12.8 and the Seller Update).
- **Buyer should want:** A separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis and buyer-knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Title and capacity are fundamental and cannot sit under a 20% general cap.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature." No fraud carve-out appears (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5).
- **Buyer should want:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. Nobody may waive this.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Insert an express non-waivable carve-out; "any nature" would capture fraud.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2 disclose "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room, the Accounts, statutory registers and public records. Schedule 7 relies on general disclosure.
- **Buyer should want:** Specific, fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Reject 1.1 and 1.2 in full. Data-room disclosure would hollow out every warranty. Note that 1.4 (non-admission) is acceptable in substance.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Buyer has no claim for any matter known to the Buyer or its advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer should want:** Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions deleted. Any qualifier must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Delete cl 8.3. "Discoverable from the data room" is the Seller's own disclosure framework restated as an exclusion.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. Consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent (cl 3/6.3). Disclosure Letter 2: no final written consent and no evidence of conditions satisfied. Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (about AUD 3.6M).
- **Buyer should want:** Effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Not consent-on-delivery. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Make effective consent plus condition evidence a condition precedent to Completion.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Approximately AUD 3.2M outstanding, to be addressed by a release "following Completion" (cl 2/7). Disclosure Letter 3: not repaid, no discharge of security.
- **Buyer should want:** A current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking and Frost's approval.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-Completion release. Require a payout letter and repayment from the funds flow, with releases effective at Completion.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 DD-005 closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. Disclosure Letter 5 says on-costs (payroll tax, super) are unaddressed.
- **Buyer should want:** A specific funds-flow line item or Seller funding, including triggered on-costs. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the silent exclusion. Add a specific line or require Seller funding, and have the Seller confirm on-costs in writing.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. This is not independent bank verification, and there is no receipt in the data room. DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of project materials on payment.
- **Buyer should want:** A broadened indemnity that preserves the SOW3 cure. Do not treat the AUD 180,000 as verified in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the narrow indemnity. Broaden it to cover IP transfer risk, keep the SOW3 cure, and require payment evidence before relying on the figure.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material" (cl 4.6/Sch 6).
- **Buyer should want:** Preserve logs, investigate, require regular updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. Disclosure records about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps), with unauthorised access and scope unresolved.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "not material" characterisation. Require log preservation, an investigation scope and written updates. Protection for this matter should be considered by the principal and not presumed either way.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)
- **Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer should want:** Assessment. The three AUD 110,000 renewals should be checked for terminability, timing and whether they are unavoidable. No automatic debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept "ordinary course" on the Seller's word. Request the contracts and assess; make no automatic price or debt adjustment.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Limitations and reliance apply to all Claims. Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime" (Seller Update, cl 12.3/13).
- **Buyer should want:** Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories kept separate. No hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. A single regime for all categories is the mechanism that undermines the title, fraud and tax protections above.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title to 100% evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012 (Disclosure Letter 10).
- **Buyer should want:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Recommendation:** Reject reliance on DD-012 alone. Require independent title searches (for example ASIC company extract, PPSR and encumbrance searches) and a Seller title and capacity warranty under the Fundamental regime.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer should want:** Tax and IP terms remain open, with no resolution and no unlimited liability assumed. A separate tax/IP regime to be proposed.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept. Keep these open and table a separate regime for principal decision.

---

**Summary of items needing Amelia Frost's decision:** the 20% cap fallback (SPA-N-001), the 18-month fallback (SPA-N-003), any post-Completion Riverlark release (SPA-N-009), and whether to seek specific protection for the DD-006 incident (SPA-N-012). None should be offered to the Seller without her written authority.
